claims.text: An NbMoCrTiAl refractory high-entropy alloy composite containing in situ TiC and Al2O3 reinforcement can be produced.
The composite exhibits excellent high-temperature mechanical properties.
The composite exhibits oxidation resistance suitable for high-temperature plasma-facing components.
The composite does not incorporate elements that produce long-lived radioactive activation.
As-cast NbMoCrTiAl has a predominantly BCC solid-solution phase.
The processing route uses extended high-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering.
The resulting composite contains approximately 32 vol.% TiC.
The resulting composite contains approximately 7 vol.% Al2O3.
The TiC and Al2O3 reinforcement particles form in situ in the NbMoCrTiAl matrix.
The ceramic particles act as second-phase barriers.
The ceramic particles refine the grain structure of the NbMoCrTiAl matrix.
Dispersed hard TiC and Al2O3 particles strengthen the alloy through second-phase strengthening.
Grain refinement and solid-solution effects enhance high-temperature mechanical strength.
Grain refinement, solid-solution effects, and ceramic reinforcement enhance oxidation resistance.
Nb, Mo, Cr, Ti, and Al avoid long-lived radioisotopes upon neutron activation and therefore meet the low-activation criterion.
The composite has approximately 50% greater compressive fracture strength than as-cast NbMoCrTiAl.
The approximately 50% compressive-strength improvement was demonstrated at room temperature, from 1010 MPa to 1542 MPa.
The composite has improved high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the as-cast alloy.
The baseline is as-cast NbMoCrTiAl without the in situ TiC and Al2O3 reinforcement phases.
Laboratory validation includes room-temperature compression and oxidation testing at approximately 800 °C.

contradictions.description: The mechanism categorically states that the selected elements meet the low-activation criterion, whereas the boundary and uncertainty fields say that activation measurements remain necessary and that the precise activation characteristics are unknown.
